pill.desc: clear, colorless to yellow solution in a single-dose prefilled pen

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability after subcutaneous injection is 74 to 89%. It is expected to be degraded into small peptides and amino acids by catabolic pathways.
clues.substance: Made by recombinant DNA technology in Chinese hamster ovary cells, with a molecular weight of about 149 kilodaltons. A sterile, preservative-free solution.
clues.product: A BLA product in 150 mg/mL pens and syringes, plus 55 mg and 180 mg syringes or cartridges; dosed at weeks 0 and 4, then every 12 weeks.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated after serious hypersensitivity to it or its excipients; upper respiratory infections and headache are among the most frequent adverse reactions.
clues.indication: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and active psoriatic arthritis in adults and children, plus Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis in adults.
clues.mechanism: Selectively binds the p19 subunit of IL-23 and inhibits its interaction with the IL-23 receptor, reducing release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines.

tell: An IL-23 p19 antibody that is 74 to 89% bioavailable subcutaneously and dosed every 12 weeks after two starter doses.
